notes: Full partition verified: 31 source and 40 target ids each covered once, with one added unit.

neither hath he power is the contested unit and survives review: neither is the rule 35 fusion of the waw with the present אֵין (giving the connective to the waw alone would leave the negative morpheme holding a positive possessive verb), and rule 43's subtraction then finds that dropping hath he loses nothing but a supplied possession and subject, so it is added.

שַׁלִּיט → that hath power is the articleless attributive recast as a relative clause (rule 41), headed on the complement under rule 44; the two אֶת markers are unrepresented under rule 16 and both assimilated articles are read on their own merits under rule 12.

בְּעָלָיו → him that is given keeps the recast relative with the noun of possession (rules 43, 46), and the suffix takes to it as the recast construct relation headed on the pronoun (rules 19, 24). All three marginal alternatives were read and set aside.
